name: Mingrelian
notes: Mingrelian (მარგალური ნინა), a Kartvelian (South Caucasian) language of western Georgia. INPUT CONTRACT: Georgian MKHEDRULI text (Unicode U+10D0..U+10FA, NFC); the historical Asomtavruli and Nuskhuri scripts and any romanisation are out of scope. Mkhedruli is a true ALPHABET — unicameral, essentially one letter per phoneme, no inherent vowel — which makes the map near-bijective. Mingrelian uses the modern Georgian letters plus three signs standard Georgian has dropped or never had: ჲ /j/, ჷ /ə/ (the schwa, prominent in the Zugdidi–Samurzaqano dialect) and ჸ /ʔ/. Like Georgian it has the three-way stop/affricate contrast voiced ~ aspirated ~ ejective. Structural ancestry node: Proto-Kartvelian (ccs.json).

sources.notes: §1.1 Phonemic System, read in full on pp. 2-3 of the manuscript's own numbering. Vowel chart i ɛ a ɔ u plus /ə/ in the Zugdid-Samurzaqan dialect; obstruents in three phonation types (voiced, voiceless aspirated, ejective) across labial, dental, alveolar, postalveolar and velar series, with a lone uvular ejective q' and glottal ʔ and h; /v/ has allophones [v] and [w]. Given in transliteration, not in Mkhedruli, so the letter-to-phoneme pairing is corroborated through the standard Georgian letter values rather than stated by Harris. One point of wording: Harris describes o as 'high-mid, back, rounded' while this spec writes ⟨ო⟩ as ɔ; her chart still places it in the mid row, so the disagreement is one of transcription convention, recorded here rather than resolved.
